system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged and confidential – internal advice

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be disregarded

Before the substantive review, one point needs flagging. The Seller's package contains a note stating that clauses marked **[STANDARD]** "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny" and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package".

That is not correct and we should not proceed on that basis:

- Nothing in our playbook or instructions records any agreement to these positions. The Seller cannot unilaterally declare a clause "cleared by both sides".
- Almost every clause tagged [STANDARD] is one where the Seller's position is **directly contrary** to our playbook (cap, thresholds, time limits, buyer knowledge, Bluefen, Riverlark). The tag has been applied precisely to the most contentious items.
- The Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] contradicts the note: "No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement."

**Recommendation:** Treat every clause as open. Our reply should expressly state that no clause has been agreed or "cleared", that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation is not accepted, and that all limitation, disclosure and condition provisions remain subject to our full mark-up.

---

## 1. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1.1 General warranty cap – Clause 12.1

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 |

**Analysis:** The Seller has opened at our *fallback* figure. The 20% position is available to us only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none has been given. We therefore have no mandate to accept it, and tactically it would be unwise to concede our fallback as the opening exchange.

**Push back:** Reinstate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is acceptable.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Recovery once basket exceeded | Excess only (deductible) | From first dollar (tipping) |

**Analysis:** Three separate departures. The de minimis is 5x our position, the basket 5x, and the Seller has converted the basket into a true deductible. On a AUD 24m deal with a known cluster of mid-sized exposures (Ironquay AUD 180k, bonuses AUD 420k, Sandbar AUD 330k, an unquantified privacy incident), a AUD 25k de minimis combined with a AUD 250k deductible could absorb a material portion of realistic claims before any recovery.

**Push back:** AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket; tipping basket (seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded).

### 1.3 Time limits and "applies to all Claims" – Clauses 12.3 / 13

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 months fallback only with Amelia Frost approval – none given) |
| Scope of limitations | "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override |

**Analysis:** As with the cap, 18 months is our unauthorised fallback. More significant is the second sentence: a default rule that every limitation applies to *all* Claims is a general-regime override that would sweep Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnity and covenant claims into the 18-month / 20% / AUD 250k regime unless we remember to carve each one out individually. This is the mechanism through which the Seller's "Fundamental/Title" and "Tax/IP" positions below are given effect.

**Push back:** 24 months for general warranty claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with the reverse: limitations in Clause 12 apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title Warranties, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations or covenants, each of which has its own regime.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Regime | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, minimum 6 years, outside basket / de minimis / knowledge bar |

**Analysis:** This is a major departure. If title to the shares fails, our loss is the entire price; a 20% cap and 18-month window would leave 80% of AUD 24m unrecoverable. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification. Note also that title is currently evidenced only by DD-012 (see 1.12), so the title warranty regime carries real weight.

**Push back:** Reject in full. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% of price, at least six years, no de minimis, no basket, no buyer-knowledge qualifier.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5

**Analysis:** Read literally, this applies caps, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to claims for **fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct**. Our playbook treats the fraud carve-out as non-negotiable ("No one may waive this"). The clause as drafted would purport to cap and time-bar a fraud claim and to exclude reliance on any fraudulent statement. Aside from being contrary to our position, such a clause is likely unenforceable in respect of fraud under NSW law, but we should not rely on that – the drafting must be fixed.

The same provision also reinforces the general-regime override in 1.3 and would extend non-reliance to the specific DD disclosures the Buyer is in fact relying on.

**Push back:** Insert an overriding carve-out: nothing in the Agreement limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller, the Company or their officers, and the caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions do not apply to such claims, to the maximum extent permitted by law. Confine 12.8 / 20.5 to general Warranty Claims.

### 1.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Disclosure standard | General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure |

**Analysis:** Disclosure Letter [1.1] and [1.2] are whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure in their purest form. Combined with the buyer-knowledge clause (1.7), the effect is that any matter buried anywhere in DD-002 to DD-012 – or on any public register – is deemed disclosed against every warranty. Paragraph [1.4] additionally reserves that nothing is an admission that any consent, payment or remediation is required, which hollows out the specific disclosures at [2]–[10].

**Push back:** Delete [1.1] and [1.2] as general disclosure. Accept only the specific disclosures at [2]–[10], and only to the extent they are fair, specific and sufficiently detailed to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Documents in the data room are disclosed only where specifically cross-referenced against an identified warranty. Reject public-register and "prudent search" disclosure.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Exclusion | No claim for any matter of which Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnity |

**Analysis:** This is the broadest form of buyer-knowledge bar: it extends to advisers' knowledge and to constructive knowledge ("discoverable"). Together with general disclosure, it effectively converts the warranty package into a search exercise against the Buyer. It would also, on its face, excuse the Seller from title and fraud claims where a "discoverable" indicator existed.

**Push back:** Delete Clause 8.3. If the Seller insists on a knowledge qualifier, it should operate only on the *Seller's* side – warranties given "so far as the Seller is aware" are qualified by reference to the actual knowledge of named Seller individuals after reasonable enquiry. No buyer-knowledge bar on title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent – Clauses 3 / 6.3

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" | Effective consent **and** evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours insufficient |

**Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue (DL [2]). The Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms that **no final written consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction** has been delivered. The Seller's drafting would allow a conditional consent to be treated as satisfied on delivery even if the 11.3 conditions were unmet and the consent could later fall away – shifting a 30% revenue risk onto the Buyer at Completion.

**Push back:** Condition precedent must be: (a) written consent from Bluefen under clause 11.2 in form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, (b) that is unconditional or whose 11.3 conditions are satisfied, with evidence of satisfaction delivered before Completion. "Reasonable endeavours" upgraded to a positive obligation to procure. Consider a specific indemnity or price adjustment if Bluefen terminates within a defined period post-Completion on grounds connected with the change of control.

### 1.9 Riverlark facility – Clauses 2 / 7

| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanism | Release "to be provided following Completion" | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release requires irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval |

**Analysis:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, with change-of-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions. DL [3] confirms not repaid and no discharge. On the Seller's draft, the Buyer would pay a debt-free price and acquire a company still encumbered, with a change-of-control default triggered at Completion and only a promise of a future release. This is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal and with the title position (see 1.12 – the shares themselves may be subject to security).

**Push back:** Require a current payout letter from Riverlark before Completion; repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow; executed deeds of release/discharge and PPSR/ASIC releases delivered at Completion. We have no authority to accept a post-Completion release; if the Seller insists, it needs an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's written approval, which does not exist.

### 1.10 Employee bonuses (DD-005) – Funds flow

**Analysis:** AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses that the Seller says are "a matter for the Seller" but which are **not itemised in the funds flow** (DL [5]). These are triggered by Completion and will fall due from the Company – i.e. from the Buyer – unless funded. The Seller has also not stated whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply; they very likely do, so the true exposure exceeds AUD 420,000.

**Push back:** Either (a) specific line item in the funds flow, deducted from the price as a debt-like item, including triggered on-costs; or (b) Seller to fund the bonuses and on-costs directly before Completion with evidence. Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Do not accept a funds flow that is silent.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1

**Analysis:** DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The Seller's indemnity is confined to the SOW3 payment. But the real risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company does not own the SOW3 Project Materials until payment is made. The narrow indemnity does not cover loss of IP, third-party claims, or costs of reprocurement.

Note the AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified either way (DL [4] concedes this), so we should not treat it as fixed.

**Push back:** Preserve the cure (payment and confirmatory assignment before Completion is the preferred route). Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of title to Ironquay Project Materials, any Ironquay claim, and reprocurement/rework costs, uncapped by the general regime. Require evidence of cleared payment and executed confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.

### 1.12 Export/privacy incident (DD-006) – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6

**Analysis:** ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; investigation preliminary; no finding yet on access, scope or notification. The Seller characterises this as "not expected to be material" – that is a conclusion the evidence does not yet support. Equally, we should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any numeric figure in the other direction.

**Push back:** Covenant to preserve logs and evidence; complete the investigation with Buyer participation; regular written updates until Completion; bring-down disclosure at Completion. A specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (including any notification, regulatory and third-party costs) sitting outside the general cap. Do not accept a bare "not material" characterisation.

### 1.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)

**Analysis:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008, DD-011) which the Seller calls ordinary-course operating costs. The Disclosure Letter concedes it does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Our playbook position is to assess, not to presume Debt or price deduction.

**Push back:** Request the underlying renewal terms, timing, termination rights and whether any amount has accrued pre-Completion. Classification (ordinary course vs. debt-like / accrued liability) to be determined on the evidence and reflected in the completion accounts mechanism if appropriate. No concession either way yet.

### 1.14 Tax / IP "settled under the general regime"

**Analysis:** The Seller asserts tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. They are not – they remain OPEN. Subjecting Tax and IP to a 20% cap, 18-month limit and AUD 250k deductible would be inappropriate; tax exposures typically run to the statutory amendment periods and IP goes to the core value of an analytics business. At the same time, we should not assume unlimited liability has been agreed.

**Push back:** State expressly that Tax and IP remain open and are not subject to the general regime by default. Propose separate regimes (tax indemnity with its own cap and period; IP warranties with a dedicated cap/period) for negotiation.

### 1.15 Title – DD-012 share register

**Analysis:** The Seller's only evidence of title is the Company's own share register. DL [10] concedes this is "the source relied on" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. An internal register is not independent proof; it does not confirm absence of encumbrances (and Riverlark security is outstanding), nor the Seller's corporate authority to sell.

**Push back:** Require independent evidence: ASIC extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, confirmation that no security over the shares exists or will be released at Completion, Seller board resolutions and (if applicable) shareholder approvals, and a Title Warranty under the separate Fundamental regime at 1.4.

### 1.16 Lower-priority items

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation only; not stated to require landlord consent. Confirm by review of the lease and build notification into pre-Completion covenants. Low risk if confirmed.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction; not on its face a change-of-control trigger on a share sale. Confirm the clause does not extend to change of control, then treat as no action.

---

## 2. Summary of recommendations

**A. Procedural**
1. Reject the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" in writing. Nothing has been agreed or cleared. All provisions remain open.

**B. Limitation package (Clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)**
2. Cap: 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not concede 20% (no Amelia Frost authority).
3. Thresholds: AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket; tipping (first-dollar) basket.
4. Time: 24 months for general claims. Do not concede 18 months (no authority).
5. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
6. Fundamental/Title: separate regime – 100% cap, minimum 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
7. Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct: unqualified carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-negotiable.
8. Tax and IP: expressly OPEN with separate regimes to be negotiated; not absorbed by the general regime.

**C. Disclosure and knowledge**
9. Delete general data-room and public-register disclosure (DL [1.1], [1.2]). Specific fair disclosure only; data-room documents disclosed only where specifically cross-referenced.
10. Delete Clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar in its entirety. No constructive-knowledge or adviser-knowledge exclusion. No knowledge bar on title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**D. Completion conditions and deliverables**
11. Bluefen: CP requiring effective consent **plus** evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery; not reasonable endeavours alone.
12. Riverlark: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds via the funds flow, and executed security releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
13. Title: independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, board/shareholder approvals, encumbrance confirmations). DD-012 alone is not accepted.
14. Ironquay: cleared SOW3 payment and confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable; broadened IP indemnity outside the general cap.

**E. Funds flow and price items**
15. DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000 plus on-costs): specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with evidence, plus shortfall indemnity. A silent funds flow is not acceptable.
16. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): obtain underlying terms before any classification; no presumption of Debt or ordinary course.

**F. Specific risk matters**
17. DD-006 export incident: log preservation, completed investigation with Buyer involvement, written updates, bring-down disclosure, and a specific indemnity outside the general cap. Do not accept "not material" or assume a breach.

**G. Internal actions**
18. Confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback authority (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) has been or will be given before the next turn of the draft.
19. Commission independent title, PPSR and ASIC searches now rather than waiting for the Seller.
20. Instruct DD team to review the lease (DD-007), Mossvale contract (DD-009) and Sandbar renewal terms (DD-008/DD-011) to close out the lower-priority points.

Please let me know if you would like me to convert this into a formal mark-up of the Seller's clauses or a reply letter to Harbourglass counsel.
=== END ADVICE ===
